register.title: PingYou Ltd's n207 certificate at 9dc93b6, issue503
register.headline: A packing of 207 squares from two placed patches of Ryan Xu's packing of 70
register.source_checks: The author reports that three exact Fraction checkers of its own, by vertex projections, by centre and support-radius separating axes and by rational polygon clipping, accept all 21,321 pairs and every wall; that its reconstruction script rebuilds every pose and the side from the n70 parent; and that this repository's sqpack exact_verify and check_rational_witness_independent, unchanged at 5b0eb012, accept its corners Witness/v2. The checkers, the reconstruction and the conversion were prepared in one workflow. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
register.credit: Credit PingYou Ltd (https://github.com/BuddenPing/square-packing-certificates) with the n207 assembly, as the source asks: two differently placed patches of Ryan Xu's n70 construction (ry-xu, issue 432), keeping 60 and 69 whole squares, with upright grids of 42 and 36 squares. The n70 patches come from Evan Daniel's exact n70 certificate (https://github.com/evand/square-packing, the regularized n-070 certificate T-146 retains), which the source credits to him for its exact retention. The source names SQUISH's n207 of issue 481 only as its comparison, and claims neither the n70 packing nor patch composition in general. The pinned source makes no statement about AI assistance; its first commit, 0d8b9c1, and the issue as first posted said that OpenAI Codex assisted the verification, the comparison review and the package, and the pinned commit, titled 'Correct attribution in submission materials', removed that sentence.
register.next_rung: Independently review the retained replay, then record source-specific adoption of the n207 side, below the ceiling T-127 holds by 7.03e-3 and below SQUISH's T-136 by 4.55e-3, with confirming evidence. Final exact-head CI remains required.
